workflow_branches.notes: Experimental KJ long-duration wrapper. It splits input video into 30s chunks, runs the existing KJ 30s workflow sequentially on one Vast instance, downloads each segment, and merges with local ffmpeg concat. It does not add a ComfyUI merge plugin and does not provide continue_motion continuity because this KJ workflow has no continue_motion input.

workflow_branches.notes: Isolated LTX2.3 self-host route for single image plus audio talking-head smoke tests. The first baseline 2043593704170070018 self-hosted successfully on RTX 3090 but was rejected twice because of pseudo subtitles/text. The current candidate uses the no-subtitle workflow 2040333916862685186; local prepare folds RunningHub helper nodes, replaces VHS_VideoCombine with CreateVideo plus SaveVideo, trims staged audio to the target duration, keeps LTX2_NAG, installs ComfyUI-KJNodes during bootstrap, and pins kornia==0.7.1 to avoid kornia_rs illegal-instruction crashes on old 3090 host CPUs. VBVR motion LoRA strength 0.60 is the current low-risk gesture preset. The branch supports a prompt-only background module through composed speaker/background/camera/guardrail prompt fields, without adding PromptRelay, Qwen3-VL, Gemini, or other prompt-generation model nodes to the self-host runtime. Direct transparent RGBA input plus background prompt is rejected after ltx23-vlbg-transparent-vbvr-20260505-03 because pseudo English subtitles reappeared; use a clean RGB anchor composed from the transparent subject and no-text background plate before the next paid smoke. V4 three-sample IDLoRA workflow 2044022005221036033 is wired through ActionMimicWorkflowSource/ActionMimicWorkflowId, but as of 2026-05-06 it has only passed local stage; paid inference was blocked by Vast account credit.

implementation_variants.description: Project-owned KJ environment image and Vast template path. The image starts from vastai/comfy:v0.19.3-cuda-12.9-py312, preinstalls KJ custom nodes, Python dependencies, records torch compatibility, and v3 validates ONNXRuntime CUDA provider plus CUDA12 runtime libraries before any KJ inference. Runtime strategy 1.2-docker-env-template uses the resulting Vast template hash while preserving R2 staging, onstart, HF speed gate, machine registry, and normal download/publish flow. The default registry is DockerHub v3. Active Vast private templates are split by GPU class: one RTX 4090 template and one RTX 3090 template.

torch_policy.core_check: torch CUDA runtime >= 12.4 and at least one CUDA device
torch_policy.auxiliary_install_policy: best-effort install missing/import-broken auxiliary packages with --no-deps matched to current torch version and current torch CUDA wheel index; if a matching auxiliary wheel is unavailable, warn and continue as long as torch core, CUDA, and GPU checks passed; do not force reinstall torch

latest_smoke.notes: DockerHub v3 pulled and started on Vast, then RemoteStopAfter=onnx_cuda passed before model downloads or /prompt. A previous GHCR v3 attempt stayed in pre-container pull; local GHCR manifest access returned 401 because the current GitHub token lacks read:packages. The passing smoke also required fixing staged ONNX smoke scripts to define output_path from sys.argv[1].

previous_v2_smoke.notes: The first v2 smoke exposed a wrong auxiliary-package CUDA index when the base image reported torch=2.11.0+cu130; V6.5.17 fixed auxiliary installs to use the current torch CUDA wheel index and to treat auxiliary install as best-effort. The follow-up smoke reached remote.validate_nodes and stopped before /prompt as intended. Curl connection reset messages appeared during large parallel downloads, but curl retries and resume completed and all model download stage markers ended successfully. Later paid KJ preprocessing showed this was not enough: ONNXRuntime CUDA provider failed to load libcublasLt.so.12 and preprocessing fell back to CPU, so v2 is no longer acceptable for further paid KJ tests.

implementation_variants.description: Single-shot KJ 30s implementation. Stages a fixed transparent-background IP image and a 30s reference video, converts the KJ canvas workflow to API JSON, disables torch compile on RTX 3090, and defaults new runs to one 481-frame 720x1280 9:16 prompt. The stage step normalizes square IP/anchor images to a vertical canvas before runtime JSON generation. It downloads the real VHS output node and publishes the result. It also runs a HuggingFace speed preflight before bootstrap and includes a 4090 candidate selector that lists 10-20 offers, short-rents 1-3 per batch, and continues to the next batch when none pass.

validated_runs.notes: Generation succeeded after disabling node 137 WanVideoTorchCompileSettings and removing WanVideoModelLoader.compile_args. The output was downloaded and manually published because the first run hit a Windows GBK vastai logs encoding issue during timing summarization; the runner was patched afterward.

implementation_variants.description: Splits videos longer than 30s into 30s chunks, stages per-segment KJ runtime workflows, runs them sequentially on one Vast instance via the existing KJ remote submit script, then downloads and ffmpeg-concats the segment outputs. New runs default to 720x1280 9:16 vertical output; square IP/anchor images are converted at stage time to a vertical canvas before the KJ runtime is prepared. Visual quality tests for portrait 9:16 outputs, including 480x848, 544x960, and 720x1280, must keep context_frames=121/context_overlap=16 and offload_img_emb/offload_txt_emb=true; context_frames=41/context_overlap=8 is only a speed smoke setting and is not valid for flicker acceptance. The current accepted fixed-scene 2.0 path is B1.1 same-frame anchor: reuse one complete person+background anchor image as ip_image.png for every 30s segment and leave WanVideoAnimateEmbeds without bg_images or mask. The separate B2 bg_images/mask experiment is retained as a failed record because it suppressed mouth/body motion. The branch also treats reference-video overlays as a probabilistic quality risk and uses preflight reference-overlay scanning plus postflight generated-artifact review before accepting long-video outputs. Cleanup roadmap: 2.0 keeps rule-based detection and targeted local cleaning; 2.1 local rules and 2.1-next OCR/LaMa samples failed on the current heavily overlaid source; next work should use clean source footage, manual cleanup, or stronger semantic/video object removal such as ProPainter/E2FGVI before any Vast inference.

kj_3_0_480p_portrait_anchor.anchor_rule: Use one complete person+background anchor image as ip_image.png and do not connect bg_images or mask.
kj_3_0_480p_portrait_anchor.notes: This is a named solution version, not a Git release and not a new workflow branch. It promotes the accepted 480x848 portrait preset for lower-cost KJ runs. The 2026-05-03 60s 30+30 reuse run generated successfully but failed user review because of localized multi-hand artifacts around 28s-31s and flicker around 43s-45s.

latest_10s_context_validation.conclusion: The 4090 10s output is stable when production 720x1280 context settings are used. Earlier flicker came from cf41 speed-test workflows, not from 4090 hardware or final playback scaling.

latest_480p_portrait_validation.conclusion: 480x848 portrait output is valid when using the same stable portrait context policy as 720x1280. Do not default 480x848 back to context_frames=241/context_overlap=32; that setting was killed during a 3090 sampling attempt.

artifact_scan.manual_interpretation: The scanner flagged red/color candidates, but spot-checked peak frames were mostly normal red shoes, lips, fingers, and chair areas. Quick self-review did not find obvious double person, double head, multi-hand, or seam break.

user_reported_issues: 28s-31s shows multi-hand / hand-structure artifacts near the 30s segment boundary.
latest_480p_portrait_60s_validation.diagnosis: The 28s-31s window crosses the 30s segment seam and the reference video around this window contains heavy subtitle, location bubble, checkmark, and sticker overlays near the body and hand zones. The 43s-45s window is inside segment 2 and the reference contains large red/black caption overlays across the torso/hand region. These are structural/temporal generation failures, not small colored-dot artifacts; they should be fixed by reference cleanup, seam-aware rerun, or affected-segment rerun rather than by simple local color inpaint.
latest_480p_portrait_60s_validation.conclusion: The current live 4090 instance can reuse the installed 480x848 KJ 3.0 environment to generate 60s as 30s+30s, but this specific 60s sample is not accepted. Keep 10s as accepted; treat 60s as pending further cleanup/rerun.

reference_overlay_cleaning.gate: Run analyzer before and after cleaning, inspect before/after contact sheet, and do not enter Vast stage/inference unless both human review and risk-after pass.

latest_local_validation.notes: The local rule cleaner removed or muted some safe upper overlays and small tokens, but near-body speech bubbles, mid-body text, and bottom subtitles remained visible or became gray blocks. This is not a valid reference for paid KJ inference.

tested_methods: thicker OCR masks and local mask variants
latest_next_validation.notes: OCR detects the Chinese overlays, but local inpaint leaves visible text, outlines, white/orange/gray blocks, or bubble frames. LaMa removes some overlays but hallucinates photovoltaic panels or semi-transparent body/clothing where text and bubbles overlap the person. Do not use this cleaned reference for KJ inference.

generated_artifact_polishing.purpose: After a merged KJ output is downloaded, run local generated-video risk detection, repair isolated colored dots or sticker specks with OpenCV inpaint, rewrap audio with FFmpeg, then run after-scan and generate before/after review sheets.
default_safety: pad each detector target by two frames to cover sub-second edge misses
attempt local silver/white halo cleanup around confirmed targets
keep cyan/blue off by default in photovoltaic scenes to avoid sky and panel false positives
not_for: large overlays that polluted pose conditioning

latest_validation.notes: v5 generalizes the repair path from red-only to detector-reported red/yellow/green/magenta candidates and adds a local silver/white halo residual mask around confirmed targets. On this sample, the safe auto-repair target remains the red hanging-ball artifact; cyan/blue stayed disabled to avoid the sky and photovoltaic panel background. A 48px halo probe removed more string/highlight residue but caused obvious blue-gray smearing on the leg edge and panel background, so it is not the default. User accepted the v5 output as good enough for now and it is the recommended polished output for this run.

validated_runs.notes: B1.1 reuses one complete person+photovoltaic-background anchor frame as ip_image.png for both 30s segments and keeps the original KJ node 171 structure without bg_images or mask. The 5s+5s smoke test restored motion, and the full 30s+30s test passed keyframes, seam, 26-30s, 48-52s, and generated-artifact review. This is the current accepted 2.0 fixed-scene path.

B2 reused the same pure seated IP image, generated bg_image.png, prompt/negative/seed, and IP-alpha-derived mask for both 30s segments. A quick structural review did not find double head or duplicate person, but detailed comparison showed mouth and body motion were nearly locked. The bg_images/mask patch over-constrained node 171, and bg_image.png contained a complete person rather than true background-only content. Do not use this B2 structure for the current KJ 2.0 path.

Initial two-segment output technically merged but failed visual review because segment 2 hallucinated a standing duplicate/background person. The live instance was kept and only segment 2 was rerun with a new seed and stronger single-seated-person prompt/negative prompt. The s01 + s02fix merge removed the duplicate person, but later review found segment 1 and segment 2 did not keep a consistent chair state, so this run is not accepted.

Two 30s segments reused the same fixed photovoltaic background prompt and the seated pure-color IP image. Quick review showed stable background and no duplicate body, but detailed review found hand-motion drift around final 49.5s-50.5s. The corresponding reference window is segment 2 19.5s-20.5s, where large sticker/location text covers the lower body and hand area. Conclusion: overlay text can contaminate KJ action/pose conditioning even when the final output does not redraw the text; clean the reference video before rerunning.

The run reused the previously accepted first 30s segment and reran only segment 2 after cleaning the 49.3s-52.0s hand-anchor overlay window in the 60s reference. The prior hand/multi-hand drift around final 49.5s-50.5s improved, but detailed review found a short-lived red point around final 29.6s near the right leg/chair area. Corresponding reference frames around 26s-30s contain red UI tokens such as checkmarks and a location bubble. Conclusion: overlay contamination is probabilistic and can manifest as extra hands, hand drift, red dots, or sticker residue; acceptances require both preflight reference-overlay review and postflight generated-artifact review.

implementation_variants.description: Split video into 10s segments, generate independently, then stitch with ffmpeg.
Adds tail-frame / continue-motion support on top of segmented v1.

Single-instance segmented implementation. Splits source video into 10s segments, carries 5 tail frames forward with continue_motion, downloads all segment outputs, and ffmpeg-concats the merged result.

Failed visual experiment. Anchors every 10s segment on the original reference image, cuts later segments with an overlap head, and merges downloaded outputs locally with ffmpeg xfade/acrossfade. It avoided v3 continue_motion identity carryover but broke cross-segment continuity because each segment re-generated a different composition.

validation_runs.notes: Initial remote submission executed only temp preview node 299 because v4 removed the required continue_motion_max_frames input. The live instance was rescued by resubmitting patched prompts that kept continue_motion_max_frames=5, removed non-save VHS preview outputs, and executed save_output node 341. The script was then patched and PrepareOnly verified. Later frame review showed the back half is unusable: s02 and s03 already re-generate the person, pose, chair, and framing differently before merge, so xfade/acrossfade cannot repair continuity.
